newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha mixed, Skikda reopening divides opinion.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha mixed, Skikda reopening divides opinion.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices turned mixed on Wednesday after gasoline's sharp gains boosted swaps values and the reopening of Algeria's Skikda port weighed slightly on physical prices, traders said.
The port's reopening after being shut for most of two weeks divided market opinion on the price impact.
Dec swaps rose $1.50 to $230.50/$231.50 while NWE cargoes slipped $2 to $228/$230 cif.

Two end-users were believed to have met some prompt demand from the delays by picking up smaller pieces in the last week, including a Spanish cargo and material from Tunisia to be shipped to Antwerp, traders said.
"If Skikda is open and stays open I think they will be more long than short and I wouldn't expect more buying in December," said one trader.
"I don't see any buyers in the situation where they have to pay up," he said.
He added that gasoline's strength and the rise in naphtha swaps to adjust the reformer spreads "is not being reflected in the physical market."
He pointed to a 6,000 tonne, open spec Russian cargo available in NWE that was on offer on Wednesday at $226 cif, down sharply from an offer of $233 yesterday.
He said the same seller was bidding for pipeline spec material on Tuesday at $232.

But another trader said the four cargoes waiting to be loaded at Skikda all had homes, so there will not be distressed cargoes at the same time the arbitrage to the U.S. has sucked material out of NWE and the Med.
"It's still relatively tight and I don't think there is much impact because the cargoes have homes," he said.
And one broker said the market did not budge.
"Skikda's open. The market hasn't reacted (because) it could be closed again tomorrow," he said.
One oil tanker was loading at Skikda, two other oil tankers were due to berth later in the day and seven others were still waiting outside the port, a port official said.
Dow Chemical fixed the World Prodigy for 27,500 tonnes out of Skikda to Northwest Europe with an option to the northern Mediterranean, for loading December 3, according to shipping sources.

Alpine and British Petroleum each fixed a tanker for 27,500 tonnes out of Ras Lanuf, Libya, to Northwest Europe with an option to the northern Mediterranean, also for loading December 3, the shipping sources said.
